# Identifier schemes and their true uniqueness scope

Measured 2026-10-11 on the dev box (native Postgres `:5432`, workspace `papercusp-workspace`) from the primary and unique keys in `pg_index` over `harness_shared`, plus the code that mints each id. Plan `scope-unique-identifiers-2026-07-26`, item P-001.

- **Scope** is the narrowest scope inside which the database guarantees that an id names exactly one thing.
- **Crosses scope** means the id is routinely quoted WITHOUT that scope: in prose, coord messages, carry notes, or an API that takes the bare id.

An id that crosses its scope is safe only if it is globally unique or the reader can recover the scope. Plan item P-002 states that as the invariant. This page is the census it rests on.

## Work-item family (one table: `harness_shared.work_items`)

| Scheme | Example | Enforced key | Crosses scope? | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Work items `WI-n` | `WI-10008270` | PK `(harness_slug, feature_id)`; unique `(workspace_id, harness_slug, feature_id)`; unique `(workspace_id, feature_id)` (`work_items_workspace_feature_id_uq`, migration 1444) | Yes: bare in prose, coord, event keys (`work-item:done:` + id), by-id tools | Minting draws from per-database disjoint ranges (P-010). Same-workspace twins were merged or removed by migration 1443 (P-011). By-id tools resolve without a harness and refuse ambiguity (P-013). Database-enforced workspace uniqueness is migration 1444, applied 2026-10-11 (P-012; its rollout gate was narrowed by `scope-unique-identifiers-2026-07-26#D-015`). |
| Engineer issues `EI-` + snowflake | `EI-25652069089571219` | same table and keys | Yes | Snowflake ids are globally unique by construction. |
| Features `F-` + kind + tail | `F-FIX-001` | same table and keys | Yes | Legacy scheme (373 rows, none created in the last 30 days at P-005 time). The live minters (`F-FIX`, `F-IDEA`) now append a time-plus-random tail from `lib/collision-resistant-id.ts`, so they cannot repeat across harnesses, workspaces or nodes (P-005, D-007). Old twins were merged by P-011. |

Since migration 1444, the database itself refuses a second row with the same `feature_id` in another harness of the same workspace. The writer fixes (P-009) and the minting change (P-010) keep such an insert from being attempted; the constraint makes any remaining attempt fail loudly instead of creating a twin.

## Plan family (`harness_plans` and its child tables)

| Scheme | Example | Enforced key | Crosses scope? | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Plan slugs | `scope-unique-identifiers-2026-07-26` | PK `(workspace_id, harness_slug, plan_slug)`: per harness | Yes: most tools and all prose take the bare slug | A slug-only lookup that matches more than one plan refuses and names the candidates; a unique slug resolves without a harness (P-006). |
| Rubric refs | `meta-acceptance-rubric` | Rubrics ARE `harness_plans` rows (`template='rubric'`), so: per harness, sharing the plan-slug namespace | Yes: `rubrics:get` accepts `harness` but does not filter by it | **Gap.** `readRubricPlanRowById` (`lib/rubrics.ts`) selects by workspace and slug with `LIMIT 1` and no harness or `ORDER BY`. Latent today: 635 rubric rows across 6 harnesses, 0 duplicate rubric slugs. Tracked as WI-6554700010008395. |
| Plan items `P-NNN` | `P-001` | PK `(workspace_id, harness_slug, plan_slug, item_id)`: per plan | Yes, constantly: bare `P-NNN` in prose and coord | `plans:items` / `plans:get` expose each item's linked, workspace-unique work-item id (P-003). A declared `plan:` + slug + `#P-NNN` ref hydrates with that work item in `coord:dispatch`, `coord:handoff` and carry briefs (P-004, D-013). A bare `P-NNN` in prose is NOT resolvable: write slug + `#P-NNN`, or the work-item id. |
| Decisions `D-NNN` | `D-012` | PK `(workspace_id, harness_slug, plan_slug, decision_id)`: per plan | Yes: bare `D-NNN` in prose | Convention only: cite slug + `#D-NNN` (the form `plans:add-decision` returns). No guard. |
| Spec clauses | `SPEC-` / `S-` ids | PK `(workspace_id, harness_slug, plan_slug, spec_id)`; revisions add `revision` | Rarely | Per plan. |
| Assertions `VAL-` | `VAL-012` | PK `(workspace_id, harness_slug, val_id)`: per harness | Sometimes | Being retired by `verification-system-improvements-2026-10-10` P-003. |

## Harness, pot and workspace identity

| Scheme | Enforced key | Crosses scope? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Harness slugs | `harness_registry` PK `workspace_id`: one registry document per workspace, so slugs are unique per workspace | Yes, across workspaces in federation | The global identity of a pot is `pots.public_key` (unique). `pots` PK is `(workspace_id, pot_home_slug)`. Retired slugs are rewritten on write by the `harness_plans_canonicalize_slug` trigger (for example `papercup` to `papercusp`). |
| Blueprints | PK `(workspace_id, harness_slug)` | No | One per harness; addressed by harness slug. |
| Docs | `harness_docs` PK `(workspace_id, harness_slug, doc_id)`; parts add `part_key` | Rarely | `docs:search` takes a harness; the engineering corpus is the default. |
| Workspace ids | No cross-host key | Yes, in federation | Workspace ids are names with no host component (for example `default` exists on many databases) [inferred from the naming; not measured across hosts]. Foreign workspaces are tracked explicitly in `p2p_foreign_workspaces`. |

## Coordination, events and system records

| Scheme | Enforced key | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Event keys and announced gate keys | `event_key_registry`, `event_key_fires` PK `(workspace_id, event_key)` | Per workspace | Keys often embed another id (`work-item:done:` + id). They are only as unique as the embedded id, which for work items means workspace-unique once P-012 lands. |
| Fleet slugs | `agent_fleets` PK `(workspace_id, fleet_slug)` | Per workspace | `@fleet:` selectors resolve inside the caller's workspace. |
| Topic slugs | `coord_topics` PK `(workspace_id, slug)` | Per workspace | |
| Routines | unique `(install_slug, name)` and `(workspace_id, install_slug, name)` | Per install | `routines:list { name }` without `installSlug` returns every install's row. |
| Reports | `report_library` PK `(workspace_id, report_id)`; `pot_reports` PK `(workspace_id, harness_slug, report_id)` | Per workspace / per harness | |
| Code recipes | `code_recipes` PK `id` | Per database (no workspace column) | |
| Coord messages | `coord_event_log` PK `id` | Per database | |
| Owner directives `#n` | `owner_directives` PK `id` (sequence) | Per database | `#1636` on one host is unrelated to `#1636` on another. |
| Test runs, tool invocations | sequence PKs | Per database | |
| Owner and session ids `su-` + uuid | UUID | Global | |
| Memory ids | `memory_canonical` PK `id` (UUID) | Global | |
| Migration numbers | `schema_migrations` PK `filename`; `migration_reservations` PK `num` | Per database, but the files are shared through git | Two databases can reserve the same number. See [migration number collisions](/internal/docs/agent-insights/migration-number-collisions-and-reservation-dx) and EI-6843. |

## Tables keyed per harness with no workspace column

These legacy consolidated tables are keyed `(harness_slug, id)` with no `workspace_id`, so an id is unique per harness across EVERY workspace in the database: `harness_issues_consolidated` (`issue_id`), `messages_consolidated`, `agent_runs_consolidated` (`run_id`), `supervisor_notes_consolidated`, `directive_summaries_consolidated`, `executed_actions_consolidated`, `harness_snapshots_consolidated`.

## How to re-measure

131 non-partial unique indexes in `harness_shared` include `harness_slug`. That population is what the P-007 recurrence guard checks. To list them, query `pg_index` joined to `pg_class` and `pg_attribute`, with `nspname = 'harness_shared'`, `indisunique`, `indpred IS NULL`, and `harness_slug` among the key columns.

To check for same-workspace work-item twins:

```sql
SELECT count(*) FROM (
  SELECT 1 FROM harness_shared.work_items
   GROUP BY workspace_id, feature_id HAVING count(*) > 1
) t;
```

## Practical rules

1. Cite work items by `WI-` / `EI-` id. After P-012 they are unique in the workspace; they are not unique across federated databases unless minted from disjoint ranges (P-010) or as snowflakes.
2. Never cite a bare `P-NNN` or `D-NNN` outside its plan. Write slug + `#P-NNN` / slug + `#D-NNN`, or the linked work-item id.
3. A plan slug or rubric ref is unique per harness. Slug-only plan lookups refuse ambiguity (P-006); rubric reads do not yet (WI-6554700010008395).
4. A sequence id (directive `#n`, coord message id, test run id) means nothing on another host.
5. Before adding a table whose text id is unique only together with `harness_slug`, decide whether the id will cross the harness boundary. If it will, key it on `workspace_id` instead.
